papers.title: Beyond the Kidney and Lung: Cutaneous and Mucosal Clues to Human Hantavirus Disease.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne viruses that cause two overlapping vascular syndromes in humans: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, including nephropathia epidemica, and hantavirus pulmonary/cardiopulmonary syndrome. Although dermatologists are rarely central to hantavirus care, early visible abnormalities may occur on the skin, mucosa, and ocular surface. This narrative review synthesizes the dermatologic and mucocutaneous manifestations of human hantavirus disease, with emphasis on signs that should prompt diagnostic suspicion in dermatology, emergency, travel-medicine, and infectious-disease settings. The dermatologic signal is strongest in hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, where facial or upper-torso flushing, conjunctival and pharyngeal injection, petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, and mucosal bleeding may appear during the febrile or hemorrhagic phases. These findings are not pathognomonic, but their diagnostic value increases when they occur with rodent or outbreak exposure, thrombocytopenia or coagulopathy, and renal abnormalities such as proteinuria, hematuria, or acute kidney injury. In hantavirus pulmonary/cardiopulmonary syndrome, particularly infections caused by New World hantaviruses, visible cutaneous involvement is less prominent and may be absent despite severe pulmonary endothelial disease. We propose a practical dermatology-oriented trigger for suspicion based on exposure history, abrupt febrile illness, nephro-pulmonary involvement, thrombocytopenia, and vascular mucocutaneous findings. Hantavirus should be considered when otherwise unexplained vascular skin or mucosal signs occur in a febrile patient with thrombocytopenia, renal involvement, hypoxemia, or compatible exposure. The skin rarely diagnoses hantavirus alone, but it may shorten time to testing, supportive care, and public-health notification.

analysis.current_state: Cutaneous signs are most evident in HFRS (flushing, conjunctival/pharyngeal injection, petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, mucosal bleeding) and are less prominent or absent in HPS caused by New World hantaviruses.
analysis.gaps: These skin findings are not pathognomonic, and their diagnostic value depends on concurrent exposure history, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, and renal abnormalities, highlighting limited specificity and paucity of systematic data.
analysis.future_research: Validation of the proposed dermatology‑oriented trigger in prospective cohorts and assessment of its impact on time to diagnosis, supportive care, and public‑health reporting are needed.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantaviruses cause HFRS and HPS. Main directions: The review synthesizes skin and mucosal signs and suggests a dermatology‑focused diagnostic trigger. Current state: Skin findings are prominent in HFRS but often absent in HPS. Gaps: Findings lack specificity and systematic evidence. Future research: Prospective validation of the trigger and its effect on diagnosis and public‑health response.

papers.title_zh: 超越肾脏和肺部:人类汉坦病毒疾病的皮肤和黏膜线索。

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒是啮齿动物传播的病毒,可导致肾综合征出血热(肾综合征出血热)和汉坦病毒肺/心肺综合征(汉坦病毒肺综合征/汉坦病毒心肺综合征)在人类中。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述聚焦于汉坦病毒感染的皮肤及黏膜表现,并为急诊、旅行医学和传染病环境中的临床医生提出以皮肤科为导向的诊断触发点。
analysis_zh.current_state: 皮肤体征在肾综合征出血热(潮红、结膜/咽部充血、点状出血、紫癜、瘀斑、黏膜出血)中最为明显,而在新世界汉坦病毒导致的汉坦病毒心肺综合征中则较不突出或缺失。
analysis_zh.gaps: 这些皮肤表现并非特征性,其诊断价值取决于同时的暴露史、血小板减少、凝血功能障碍和肾脏异常,凸显特异性有限且系统性数据稀缺。
analysis_zh.future_research: 需要在前瞻性队列中验证所提出的皮肤科导向触发点,并评估其对诊断时间、支持治疗以及公共卫生报告的影响。

papers.title: Characteristics and Superspreading Potential of Andes Virus Person-to-Person Transmission.
papers.abstract: By using historical contact tracing data, we estimated that 23.4% of case-patients caused 80% of Andes virus (ANDV) person-to-person transmission. We demonstrated a low but nonnegligible probability of observing a large-scale ANDV infection outbreak in a rodent-free setting consisting of close contacts, despite the historically self-limited person-to-person transmission of ANDV.

papers.full_text: Volume 32, Number 10—October 2026 Dispatch Characteristics and Superspreading Potential of Andes Virus Person-to-Person Transmission Cite This Article Citation for Media Abstract By using historical contact tracing data, we estimated that 23.4% of case-patients caused 80% of Andes virus (ANDV) person-to-person transmission. We demonstrated a low but nonnegligible probability of observing a large-scale ANDV infection outbreak in a rodent-free setting consisting of close contacts, despite the historically self-limited person-to-person transmission of ANDV. Hantaviruses are rodentborne zoonotic enveloped RNA viruses belonging to the family Hantaviridae (1). The genus Orthohantavirus, which belongs to the subfamily Mammantavirinae, is the only genus in Hantaviridae that can cause disease in humans (1). Infections in humans occur mainly through inhalation of aerosolized excreta from infected rodents, which can lead to hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, a severe respiratory disease with a case-fatality rate of up to 50% in the Americas, depending on the infecting hantavirus type (2). Although uncommon, person-to-person transmission of Andes virus (ANDV), a member of the genus Orthohantavirus, has been documented in South America in recent decades, typically in high-intensity close-contact settings, such as households and social gatherings (3–9). On May 2, 2026, an ANDV outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship was reported to the World Health Organization (WHO), with the first case illness onset on April 3 (10). Subsequent epidemiologic investigations proposed a working hypothesis that person-to-person transmission originated from a seed case in a person who probably acquired infection through environmental exposure during travel in Argentina before boarding the ship on April 1 (10). By July 2, a total of 13 ANDV cases had been identified, including 12 laboratory-confirmed and 1 probable case; 3 of those cases were fatal (10). According to the initial WHO notification for the outbreak on May 2, public health and control measures, including contact tracing, case isolation, clinical care, and medical evacuation of symptomatic passengers, had been implemented onboard the ship (11). By using historical contact tracing data, we aimed to estimate key epidemiologic characteristics of person-to-person transmission of ANDV, including the serial interval (SI) distribution and transmission heterogeneity, given that those traits strongly shape outbreak size. We conducted a literature review of historical ANDV outbreak investigations and extracted contact tracing data from ANDV case clusters that involved person-to-person transmission events. We only included studies conducted in Argentina, given that the seed case-patient of the 2026 outbreak was most likely infected there, according to the WHO report (10). We identified 5 eligible studies that provided detailed contact histories and viral genetic evidence strongly supporting person-to-person transmission and linking infections to specific viral lineages or strains (3–7). We extracted symptom onset dates to calculate the SI and compiled case-cluster sizes to estimate the effective reproduction number (Rt) and transmission heterogeneity measured by a dispersion parameter (k) (12). In case-clusters, we considered terminal cases and sporadic cases attributed to environmental exposure but with no documented human contact as generating no secondary infections. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate the epidemiologic parameters while accounting for random effects attributable to epidemiologic differences among ANDV lineages or strains during different epidemic periods. We further conducted a branching process simulation study to assess the transmission potential of the current outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship on the basis of the pooled estimates of epidemiologic parameters, considering a plausible range of the initial Rt for ANDV (Appendix). We identified a total of 88 case-clusters from the included studies, among which 50 (56.8%) were not associated with any secondary person-to-person transmission events. After accounting for variations across lineages or strains, the pooled estimate of Rt was 0.74 (95% credible interval [CrI] 0.28–1.29) and the estimate of k was 0.64 (95% CrI 0.36–1.16). Apart from inherent differences among ANDV lineages or strains, the substantial variation in Rt across lineages or strains could also be attributed to differences in study settings and individual-level heterogeneity in reproduction numbers (5). We estimated that 23.4% (95% CrI 15.1%–30.3%) of the cases generated 80% of the transmission events, suggesting the person-to-person spread of ANDV exhibited relatively high heterogeneity, although it appeared lower than that observed for other pathogens known for superspreading events, including SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus, and Ebola virus (13,14). Among 38 case-clusters that involved secondary transmissions, we identified 76 primary–secondary transmission pairs with available symptom onset dates, which enabled us to calculate the SI. We estimated a pooled mean SI of 21.92 (95% CrI 18.97–25.78) days and an SD of 6.98 (95% CrI 5.80–8.66) days. Although we observed little variation in the SI distributions across lineages or strains, our estimates are conditional on reported case-clusters and might not represent the full population-level distribution of ANDV infections. That condition is particularly relevant given that only 1 transmission pair was identified for the ANDV Cent BsAs lineage (Figure 1). Assuming the initial reproduction number of the current ANDV outbreak lies within the 0.4–2.5 range (3) (Appendix Figure 1), together with the pooled SI and k estimates from historical data, we simulated plausible outbreak trajectories under a stochastic branching process framework. On the basis of the assumption that effective control measures were implemented after the WHO notification dated May 2, 2026 (11), we assumed the Rt decreased from that date onward (Appendix). Within 10 weeks after symptom onset of the seed case, 95% of the simulation results produced <15 cumulative cases of ANDV infection (Figure 2). We estimated the probability of sustained transmission after 1 generation of spread to be 20.9% (95% CrI 5.3%–37.4%) for historical ANDV infection clusters and 28.6% (95% CrI 10.0%–57.4%) using the assumed initial reproduction numbers of the ANDV infection outbreak on the cruise ship (Figure 3). In sensitivity analyses, excluding sporadic cases from historical clusters yielded results similar to those of the main analysis (Appendix Figure 2). The absence or delayed implementation of control measures would increase the likelihood of a large-scale outbreak, under the assumption that such measures effectively reduce the reproduction number (Appendix Figure 3). Because only 8 cases occurred within approximately 1 mean SI after the putative seed case-patient’s symptom onset (18–25 days) before the initial WHO notification on May 2, 2026, conventional methods cannot reliably estimate the initial reproduction number without support of contact tracing data. Nonetheless, we used a branching process simulation model with transparent assumptions to illustrate plausible epidemic trajectories for the ANDV outbreak. We noted that person-to-person transmission of ANDV in the general community might be close to the situations of historical ANDV outbreaks, where we observed mostly self-limited risks. Timely and accurate identification of ANDV infection is critical yet challenging because of the nonspecific nature of early symptoms, which necessitates systematic risk assessment for symptomatic persons and their contacts. A key limitation of this study was its reliance on self-reported contact histories and symptom onset dates derived from publicly available data sources. Potential misclassification of epidemiologic links attributable to unreported co-exposures to rodents, underdetection of subclinical or asymptomatic infections caused by terminal cases, and recall bias in symptom onset might have affected the parameter estimates (15). Of note, no clear evidence supporting transmission from asymptomatic or presymptomatic case-patients currently exists. In the simulation study, we anchored control measures to the symptom onset date of the seed case-patient, thereby overlooking the biological delay imposed by the incubation period. In summary, our results provide insights into the person-to-person transmission potential of ANDV, which exhibited substantial heterogeneity. We found a low but significant chance of observing a relatively large-scale ANDV outbreak in a rodent-free setting consisting of close contacts, which might be eradicated across a few generations of person-to-person transmission. Because no vaccine or antiviral treatment for ANDV infection is currently available, continuous surveillance of person-to-person transmission risk of ANDV is essential for preparedness against future outbreaks. analysis.methods: The authors reviewed Argentine ANDV outbreak reports, extracted historical contact‑tracing data on symptom onset, and used a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate Rt, dispersion (k), and serial interval, then applied stochastic branching‑process simulations to the 2026 cruise‑ship outbreak.
analysis.results: They estimated that 23.4% (95% CrI 15.1–30.3%) of cases generated 80% of transmission events; pooled Rt = 0.74 (95% CrI 0.28–1.29) and k = 0.64 (95% CrI 0.36–1.16); mean serial interval = 21.92 days (SD = 6.98); and the simulated probability of sustained transmission after one generation was 20.9% for historical clusters and 28.6% for the cruise‑ship scenario.
analysis.contribution: The study quantifies superspreading potential and outbreak risk for ANDV, informing surveillance and control strategies, and shows that delayed or absent measures could raise the likelihood of a large‑scale outbreak.
analysis.limitations: Findings are based on limited historical clusters, with some lineages represented by only one transmission pair, and the initial reproduction number of the cruise‑ship outbreak could not be directly measured.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Andes virus can cause severe hantavirus pulmonary syndrome with up to 50% fatality, and although person-to-person spread is uncommon, it occurs in close-contact settings, raising outbreak concerns. Methods: Researchers reviewed Argentine outbreak reports, extracted historical contact‑tracing data, applied a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate Rt, dispersion (k), and serial interval, and simulated outbreak trajectories for the 2026 cruise‑ship event. Results: They found 23.4% (95% CrI 15.1–30.3%) of cases caused 80% of transmission; pooled Rt = 0.74 (95% CrI 0.28–1.29), k = 0.64 (95% CrI 0.36–1.16); mean serial interval = 21.92 days (SD = 6.98); and a 20.9%–28.6% chance of sustained transmission after one generation. Contribution: The work quantifies ANDV superspreading potential and outbreak risk, guiding surveillance and control measures, and highlights that delayed interventions increase large‑outbreak risk. Limitations: Estimates rely on limited historical clusters, some lineages have only one transmission pair, and the initial reproduction number for the cruise‑ship outbreak was not directly observed.

papers.title: Could bradykinin pathway inhibition change the course of severe hantavirus disease?
papers.abstract: A recent multi-country hantavirus outbreak associated with a cruise ship underscores the urgent need to understand the mechanisms driving severe vascular leakage and multi-organ failure. While disease severity is largely attributed to a dysregulated host immune response and intense cytokine surge, the precise molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Laboratory evidence indicates that hantavirus infection activates the factor XII-dependent kallikrein-kinin system, leading to elevated bradykinin production and subsequent endothelial barrier dysfunction. This translational mechanism is tentatively supported by two clinical case reports where severe hantavirus infections were successfully treated with the bradykinin receptor antagonist icatibant. We hypothesize that exaggerated bradykinin signalling drives the vascular leak phenotype, making the kallikrein-kinin pathway a compelling therapeutic target. Ultimately, effectively combating hantavirus-induced vascular permeability may require a multi-faceted approach combining targeted bradykinin inhibition with broader immunomodulatory strategies.

papers.title_zh: 抑制缓激肽通路能否改变严重汉坦病毒疾病的进程?

analysis_zh.background: 近期一次跨多国的汉坦病毒疫情在邮轮上爆发,凸显亟需了解严重血管渗漏和多器官衰竭的机制;疾病严重程度主要归因于宿主免疫反应失调和细胞因子风暴,但具体分子介质仍未完全阐明。
analysis_zh.methods: 在提供的证据中未报告。
analysis_zh.results: 实验室证据表明汉坦病毒感染激活第十二因子依赖的激肽酶-激肽系统,导致缓激肽产生升高并引起内皮屏障功能障碍;两例临床病例报告描述了使用缓激肽受体拮抗剂伊卡替班成功治疗严重的汉坦病毒感染。
analysis_zh.contribution: 作者假设过度的缓激肽信号传导驱动血管渗漏表型,使激肽酶-激肽通路成为有吸引力的治疗靶点,并指出有效治疗可能需要将缓激肽抑制与更广泛的免疫调节策略相结合。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅有摘要可得;证据仅限于实验室发现和两例病例报告,缺乏系统的临床试验数据。

papers.title: Geometrical study of DNA sequences of New World hantavirus and Nipah virus using the ATG genomic walk method
papers.abstract: Viral genome analysis is essential for characterizing genetic variation and evolutionary patterns, while complementary computational approaches may provide additional insights beyond conventional sequence-based methods. In this paper, the complete RNAs of New World hantavirus and Nipah virus are analyzed using a DNA walk method that traces the distribution of ATG triplets along sequences. It provides visual one-dimensional models (ATG trajectories) of genomes on a plane and quantitative estimates based on: (i) point-defined relative values of the divergence of ATG trajectories, (ii) relative global-defined standard deviation of ATG triplet numbers in a studied set of sequences, and (iii) relative global-defined standard deviation of fractal dimension values of inter-ATG distances in the same sequence set. These calculated parameters for the two species mentioned are compared with those of previously studied viruses, allowing them to be arranged in the following order based on their increasing sensitivity to variations in ATG distribution: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2, Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus, Nipah, Ebola, and dengue viruses, which is in good accordance with their observed and recognized mutability. The method verified in this paper can be used as a supplementary pre-screening qualitative and quantitative tool for conventional sequencing analysis.

papers.title_zh: 利用ATG基因组步行方法对新世界汉坦病毒和尼帕病毒DNA序列的几何学研究

analysis_zh.background: 病毒基因组分析对于表征遗传变异和进化模式至关重要,补充的计算方法可能在传统基于序列的方法之外提供额外的洞见。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用 DNA 步进(ATG 基因组步进)方法,对新世界 汉坦病毒 和尼帕病毒的完整 RNA 进行分析,该方法追踪序列中 ATG 三联体的分布。
analysis_zh.results: 该方法生成了可视化的一维 ATG 轨迹,并提供了以下定量估计:(i) ATG 轨迹的相对发散度,(ii) ATG 三联体数量的全局标准差,(iii) ATG 间距分形维度值的全局标准差;依据对 ATG 分布的敏感性对病毒进行的比较排序与已知的变异性相吻合(SARS‐CoV‐2、MERS‐CoV、尼帕、埃博拉、登革热)。

papers.title: Хантавірусна інфекція: епідеміологія, шляхи передачі, сучасні підходи до лікування, ситуація в Україні та Європі Hantavirus infection: epidemiology, transmission routes, current treatment approaches, and the situation in Ukraine and Europe
papers.abstract: Хантавірусна інфекція залишається актуальною проблемою для країн Європи та України попри відносно невисоку загальну захворюваність. Основним джерелом цього збудника є мишоподібні гризуни, найчастіше зараження людини відбувається аерогенним шляхом під час інгаляції пилу, контамінованого сечею, фекаліями або слиною інфікованих тварин. У країнах Європи переважають форми які асоційовані з геморагічною гарячкою та нирковим синдромом, спричинені вірусом Puumala, рідше – Dobrava, Seoul та Tula. За даними ECDC, у 2023 р. у 28 країнах ЄС/ЄЕЗ зареєстровано 1885 випадків, причому найвищі показники відзначалися у Фінляндії та Німеччині – 60,5% усіх повідомлених випадків. Дані літературних джерел свідчать, що в Європі серопревалентність хантавірусної інфекції в загальній популяції становить близько 2,98%, а в групах професійного ризику – є вищою. В Україні відкриті джерела вказують на незначну реєстрацію випадків, імовірну недооцінку поширеності та обмеженість систематизованих публічних епідеміологічних даних. Діагностика базується насамперед на серологічних методах із використанням молекулярних тестів. Специфічної широко схваленої етіотропної терапії для Європи наразі немає, лікування залишається переважно підтримувальним та включає респіраторну, гемодинамічну та ниркову підтримку. Перспективними напрямами є удосконалення діагностики, посилення епіднагляду та розвиток вакцинних платформ.

analysis.background: Hantavirus infection remains a relevant problem for Europe and Ukraine despite relatively low overall incidence.
analysis.methods: Not reported in the supplied evidence.
analysis.results: In Europe, disease is dominated by hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome caused by Puumala virus, with occasional Dobrava, Seoul and Tula viruses. In 2023, 28 EU/EAA countries reported 1,885 cases, with Finland and Germany accounting for 60.5% of cases. Seroprevalence in the general European population is about 2.98%, higher among occupational risk groups. Ukraine reports few cases, likely under‑estimated due to limited systematic epidemiological data.
analysis.contribution: The paper highlights the need to improve diagnostics, strengthen surveillance, and develop vaccine platforms for hantavirus infection in Europe.
analysis.limitations: Only an abstract is available, so detailed methods, full data sets, and comprehensive analysis are not provided.

papers.title: Expanded protocadherin-1 usage reveals a broader hantavirus entry landscape.
papers.abstract: Mammalian hantaviruses are RNA viruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia. The cellular entry mechanisms of most hantaviruses remain poorly defined. To examine entry by phylogenetically distinct hantaviruses identified across Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, we generated replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing Gn/Gc proteins from Necoclí, Sangassou, Thottapalayam, Kenkeme, Nova, Oxbow, and Tula viruses. All these Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme supported infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. Except for rVSV-Kenkeme, these rVSVs did not acquire additional mutations beyond pre-engineered rescue-enhancing changes during rescue and passaging. Genetic studies in human cells lacking protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) showed that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses use PCDH1 for efficient infection, although the Nova phenotype was weaker. These three Gn/Gc proteins bound soluble PCDH1 with different apparent avidities, and infection by the corresponding rVSVs was inhibited by soluble PCDH1; Necoclí and Tula, but not Nova, were also blocked by a PCDH1-targeting monoclonal antibody. Authentic Tula virus infection was similarly reduced in PCDH1 knockout endothelial cells. Finally, the broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc human monoclonal antibody ADI-42898 efficiently neutralized Necoclí, Nova, Sangassou, and Kenkeme rVSVs, but showed weak or undetectable activity against Oxbow, Tula, and Thottapalayam rVSVs. Together, these findings expand the range of hantavirus glycoproteins capable of mediating infection of human endothelial cells, broaden the phylogenetic scope of PCDH1-dependent entry, and identify receptor-targeted and viral glycoprotein-targeted strategies with differential activity.IMPORTANCEMany newly discovered hantaviruses are known only from sequence data, leaving their ability to enter human cells and their receptor usage unresolved. Using a BSL2-compatible recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) system, we show that glycoproteins from several divergent hantaviruses can mediate infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. We also show that protocadherin-1 (PCDH1), previously linked mainly to New World hantaviruses, is used by Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses but not universally across the panel, revealing broader but heterogeneous receptor usage. An authentic Tula virus experiment supports this conclusion beyond the surrogate system. Finally, a broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc antibody neutralizes several, but not all, of these viruses, highlighting both the promise and the limits of broadly protective countermeasures and the utility of these rVSVs for evaluating entry inhibitors.

source_records.abstract: Mammalian hantaviruses are RNA viruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia. analysis.background: Mammalian hantaviruses cause severe cardiopulmonary and renal syndromes (A1) and the cellular entry mechanisms of most hantaviruses remain poorly defined (A2). The study addresses the gap that many newly discovered hantaviruses are known only from sequence data, leaving their human cell entry and receptor usage unresolved (A11).
analysis.methods: The authors generated replication‑competent recombinant VSVs bearing Gn/Gc proteins from seven divergent hantaviruses (A3) and used primary human endothelial cells, PCDH1‑knockout human cells, soluble PCDH1, and monoclonal antibodies to assess entry (A6, A9).
analysis.results: All Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme mediated infection of primary human endothelial cells (A4). Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses required PCDH1 for efficient infection (A6), bound soluble PCDH1 with varying avidities and were inhibited by soluble PCDH1 (A7). A PCDH1‑targeting monoclonal antibody blocked Necoclí and Tula but not Nova (A8), and authentic Tula infection was reduced in PCDH1‑KO cells (A9). A broadly reactive anti‑Gn/Gc antibody neutralized several rVSVs but not others (A10).
analysis.contribution: These findings expand the known range of hantavirus glycoproteins that can infect human endothelial cells (A12), reveal broader but heterogeneous PCDH1 usage beyond New World viruses (A13), validate the observations with authentic Tula virus (A14), and demonstrate the potential and limits of broadly reactive antibodies for countermeasures (A15).
analysis.limitations: The work is limited to an abstract, relies on a BSL‑2‑compatible rVSV surrogate system rather than live hantaviruses for most viruses (A3, A12), and therefore may not capture all aspects of natural infection.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantaviruses cause severe disease and most entry mechanisms are unknown, especially for newly sequenced strains (A1, A2, A11). Methods: Researchers built rVSVs with Gn/Gc from seven hantaviruses and tested entry in primary human endothelial cells, PCDH1‑knockout cells, and with soluble PCDH1 or antibodies (A3, A6, A9). Results: All but Kenkeme entered endothelial cells; Necoclí, Tula, and Nova required PCDH1, showed variable binding to soluble PCDH1, and were differentially blocked by antibodies; authentic Tula infection was reduced in PCDH1‑KO cells; a broad anti‑Gn/Gc antibody neutralized several but not all viruses (A4, A6‑A10). Contribution: The study broadens the hantavirus entry landscape, identifies heterogeneous PCDH1 usage, validates findings with authentic virus, and highlights both promise and limits of broad antibodies (A12‑A15). Limitations: Only an abstract and a surrogate rVSV system were used, limiting insight into full viral biology (A3, A12).

papers.title_zh: 扩展的protocadherin-1利用揭示了更广泛的 汉坦病毒 进入格局。

analysis_zh.background: 哺乳动物汉坦病毒可导致严重的心肺和肾综合征 (A1),且大多数汉坦病毒的细胞进入机制仍未明确 (A2)。本研究弥补了许多新发现的汉坦病毒仅通过序列数据已知、其在人类细胞中的进入方式及受体使用尚未解析的空白 (A11)。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者构建了携带七种不同汉坦病毒 Gn/Gc 蛋白的可复制重组 VSV(A3),并使用原代人类内皮细胞、PCDH1 基因敲除人细胞、可溶性 PCDH1 以及单克隆抗体评估病毒进入 (A6, A9)。
analysis_zh.results: 除 Kenkeme 外,所有 Gn/Gc 蛋白均可介导原代人内皮细胞感染 (A4)。Necoclí、Tula 和 Nova 病毒的高效感染依赖 PCDH1 (A6),它们以不同亲和力结合可溶性 PCDH1,且被可溶性 PCDH1 抑制 (A7)。针对 PCDH1 的单克隆抗体阻断了 Necoclí 和 Tula,但未阻断 Nova (A8),在 PCDH1‐KO 细胞中真实的 Tula 病毒感染亦被降低 (A9)。一种广谱抗 Gn/Gc 抗体中和了若干 rVSV,但未中和其他病毒 (A10)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 这些发现扩展了已知可感染人类内皮细胞的汉坦病毒糖蛋白范围 (A12),揭示了除新世界病毒外更广泛但异质的 PCDH1 使用情况 (A13),并通过真实的 Tula 病毒验证了上述观察 (A14),同时展示了广谱抗体在防御中的潜力与局限 (A15)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 本研究仅限于摘要,且对大多数病毒使用 BSL‐2 兼容的 rVSV 替代体系而非活体汉坦病毒,因此可能未涵盖自然感染的全部特征 (A3, A12)。
